title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: continuous batching currently groups requests by arrival time which can produce high padding overhead when sequence length variance is large. This change introduces sequence-length bucketing with an adaptive padding minimization heuristic to improve token throughput and GPU utilization while preserving latency SLOs. The implementation adds a light-weight estimator for incoming request length distribution, a bucketing scheduler that forms batches with similar seq-lens, and an option to trade a small extra queueing delay for reduced padding when beneficial. It also wires the heuristic into the KV-cache warmup path so that requests expected to share prefixes are co-batched when possible. This PR includes runtime changes, scheduler unit tests, end-to-end microbenchmarks, and documentation for the new config knobs. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan and canary gating.

review_comments: Carlos Mendes: Nice approach, can you clarify how the timeout vs padding tradeoff is tuned in prod? Suggest exposing percentile-based knobs instead of fixed thresholds.
Aisha Patel: Responded that defaults are adaptive: the estimator tracks p50/p90 p99 seq-lens and scales bucket boundaries accordingly; config exposed as percentiles and max-delay-ms.
Evelyn Zhou: Found a race in continuous_batcher where a bucket refill could interleave with shutdown; requested a graceful drain test.
Aisha Patel: Added a drain guard and included a unit test that simulates shutdown under load (test included).
Ravi Kumar: Observed a small regression in 99th percentile latency on short-seq workloads in first run; asked for benchmark details.

Aisha Patel: Investigated and found default bucket size was too aggressive for <8-token requests; tuned heuristics and re-ran benchmarks - 99p latency returned to baseline while throughput improved for mixed workloads.
ci_summary: CI run #1: lint + unit tests passed, perf-check failed on mixed-workload job (99p latency regression)
CI run #2: fixes applied, unit tests passed, perf-check passed (throughput +12% on open-domain chat mix, padding reduced ~28%)
Canary: rolled out to perf-canary pool for 24h with no errors and expected gains
benchmark_results: Open-domain chat mix (50/30/20 short/medium/long): throughput +12% token/sec, padding tokens reduced 28%, 99p latency unchanged
Search/short-query mix (<8 tokens): throughput +6% after heuristic tuning, 99p latency within 2% of baseline
Long-context streaming (>=1024 tokens): unchanged throughput, reduced memory pressure on KV cache due to affinity grouping
ops_notes: Rollout plan: enable on low-traffic regions for 48h, monitor batching.padding_ratio, gpu_util, and tail latency dashboards
Fallback: if batching.padding_ratio increases or 99p latency regresses >5% revert to continuous batching via feature flag
release_notes: Introduce sequence-length bucketing for continuous batching to reduce padding and improve token throughput; adds configurable padding-delay tradeoff and KV-cache affinity hooking. Recommended canary rollout and monitoring of tail latency and padding metrics.
